findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Various items that are packaged in house lacked specific label information. These items included packaged breads, veggies, seafood, etc. in many coolers, freezers, and shelves throughout the facility. Discussed with the PIC the required label information: common name of food, list of ingredients, name and place of business of manufacturer/distributor, and food source for each major food allergen. Ensure that the necessary information is included on packaged labels.
findings.citation_text: 3-602.11(A) Food Labels. (A) FOOD PACKAGED in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, shall be labeled as specified in LAW, including 21 CFR 101 - Food labeling, and 9 CFR 317 Labeling, marking devices, and containers.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed two packages of smoked Salmon stored in a floor reach cooler to exceed the 7-day holding timeframe. The packaging dates were 3/08/2025 and 3/14/2025. The items were pulled and discarded by the PIC. Ensure that cooked meats are never held in house longer than 7 days of preparation. If the 7-day time frame is exceeded, be sure to discard food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed employee health reporting agreements were not available for three of the four people working at the time of inspection. Employee health documents were provided and discussed. Reporting agreements were signed by staff during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution at 3 part sink was observed around 100-150ppm after preparation. Quat tablets used require a concentration of 200ppm. Additional tablets were added to provide proper concentration. Ensure all staff are using the appropriate number of sanitizer tablets based on the amount of water when preparing solutions.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed eggs stored above bell peppers in the display cooler. Ensure eggs are stored below vegetables and ready to eat foods.  The eggs were moved during the inspection. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed no test strips available during the inspection. Test strips were ordered during the inspection. Additionally, test strips were given to the manager in case they were needed before the order arrived. 
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. The mop was stored inside the mop bucket. The mop was moved into a correct position during the inspection. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.
